subject: Dressing-room storage that feels calm
hook: Spare room to dressing room: the six decisions in between.
ig:
Spare room to dressing room: the six decisions in between. Here's how a typical project runs.

The spare bedroom is the most common room we're asked to turn into a dressing room. It's a good fit — but every room has awkward bits.

The window decides where the dressing table goes. The radiator decides where tall units can't. The door swing decides whether the first wardrobe needs sliding doors. And whether the room still has to sleep a guest decides almost everything else.

So the order matters: brief, survey, layout, 3D review, then manufacture in our own workshop and installation by our own team. Nothing gets cut until you've seen it and signed off the itemised quote.

Swipe for the full sequence. Got a spare room in mind? Send us a DM with a rough sketch and we'll tell you what's possible.
fb:
Got a spare bedroom that's mostly a dumping ground? It's the room we're asked to turn into a dressing room more than any other.

This carousel walks through how a typical project runs — and the questions that come up along the way. Where does the radiator sit? Which way does the door open? Does it still need to fit a guest bed occasionally?

Answer those early and the rest falls into place. We design with you in 3D, make everything in our Hanley workshop and fit it ourselves. Have a look at our walk-in wardrobe page for more.

cta: DM us a rough sketch of your spare room
alt: Six frames showing a survey sketch, a 3D design on a laptop, cut panels, carcass assembly, a level check and a finished room handover (AI concept images).
on_asset: F1: The brief — Who uses the room, what they own, and whether it still needs to sleep a guest now and then. | F2: The survey — We measure every wall and note the window, radiator, door swing and sockets, because each one shapes where storage can go. | F3: The layout — A typical plan runs hanging along the longest wall, drawers and a dressing table near the window light, doors kept clear of the entrance. | F4: The 3D review — You see it in 3D and change finishes, handle style and section sizes before anything is cut. | F5: Workshop and fit — Panels cut, edged and assembled in our Hanley workshop, checked, then installed and scribed to the walls by our own team. | F6: Handover — Every drawer and door adjusted and shown to you. Concept images throughout.
